sourcedFrom: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) (not printed)
cleanIntro: The 500 Bullpup is a Model 500 pump action inside a two-piece plastic bullpup stock, and that changes how it comes apart. The barrel comes off the same way as on any 500 - takedown screw, bolt in the middle of the ejection port. Everything past that means splitting the stock enclosure and lifting the action out, and Mossberg's book warns at that point that further disassembly takes some expertise, so it lives in Deep Clean. Two safeties matter here: the crossbolt on the trigger guard (pushed fully to the right is SAFE) and a grip safety; inside the stock there is also a safety button on the top rear of the receiver itself.

steps.title: Crossbolt safety fully to the right - SAFE
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, fingers away from the trigger. Push the crossbolt safety from the left side of the trigger guard until it is fully to the right, the ejection-port side.
steps.prose: Fully to the right is the only SAFE position. The red ring on the crossbolt is a training aid, not a signal that the gun is safe.
steps.quote: Move the crossbolt safety button (Fig. 3) to the "on" or "safe" (fully to the right) position.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — UNLOADING, PDF p.6

steps.title: Lock lever down, forend back slowly - chambered shell out by hand
steps.action: Press the action release lock lever on the left side of the buttstock and draw the forend rearward slowly until the chambered shell is fully out and visible in the ejection port. Lift it out by hand.
steps.prose: Slowly, so the shell stops in the port where you can take it, rather than being thrown.
steps.quote: Depress the action release lock lever (Fig. 4C) and pull the forend rearward, slowly, until the live shotshell is completely withdrawn and visible in the ejection port. Remove shotshell by hand.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — UNLOADING, PDF p.6

steps.title: Keep pulling - next shell onto the elevator, roll it out the port
steps.action: Keep drawing the forend back until the next shell drops onto the elevator, then roll the shotgun on its side so that shell falls out through the ejection port.
steps.prose: The ejection port is on the right. Roll the gun toward it and catch the shell.
steps.quote: Continue pulling the forend rearward to release the next shotshell onto the elevator. Roll the shotgun sideways to allow the released shotshell to drop out through the ejection port.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — UNLOADING, PDF p.6

steps.title: Forend forward, gun over, right thumb on the cartridge stop
steps.action: Push the forend completely forward. Turn the gun over so the trigger guard faces up, still pointed somewhere safe. Put your right thumb into the opening in the bottom of the receiver and press the cartridge stop on the right side; the shells come out one at a time. Repeat until the magazine tube is empty.
steps.prose: One shell per press. Count them against what you loaded.
steps.quote: Push the forend completely forward. Turn the shotgun over so that the trigger guard is positioned upward and the gun remains pointed in a safe direction. Insert right thumb into the opening in the bottom of the receiver and depress the cartridge stop on the right side (Fig. 8) to release shotshells one at a time. Repeat until all shotshells are removed from the magazine tube.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — UNLOADING, PDF p.6

steps.title: Action open, look again at chamber, elevator and tube
steps.action: Pull the forend completely rearward and look into the chamber, at the elevator and into the magazine tube once more. Leave the action open and the crossbolt fully to the right.
steps.prose: The elevator is the place a shell hides after a partial unload. Look at it, do not assume.
steps.quote: Pull the forend completely rearward. Visually inspect chamber, elevator and magazine tube again to insure that no shotshells remain in the shotgun.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — UNLOADING, PDF p.6
steps.warn: Leave the action in the open, rearward position and the crossbolt safety button in the "on" or "safe" (fully to the right) position.

steps.title: Crossbolt SAFE, action open, barrel and tube checked
steps.action: With the crossbolt safety fully to the right, press the action release lock lever and slide the forend fully rearward. Check the barrel, chamber and magazine tube once more before anything comes off.
steps.prose: The crossbolt is the button in front of the trigger guard.
steps.quote: Depress the action release locklever and open the action by sliding the forend fully rearward. Inspect the barrel, chamber and magazine tube to insure that the shotgun is unloaded.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — BARREL REMOVAL, PDF p.7

steps.title: Forend forward until the bolt face sits mid-port
steps.action: Move the forend slowly forward from fully rearward and stop when the front of the bolt is in the middle of the ejection port.
steps.prose: That is the position the barrel comes off in - not fully open and not closed.
steps.quote: Move the forend slowly forward from the fully rearward position until the front of the bolt is in the middle of the ejection port
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — BARREL REMOVAL, PDF p.7

steps.title: Takedown screw counter-clockwise until it is free of the tube
steps.action: Turn the takedown screw at the muzzle end of the magazine tube counter-clockwise until its threads are completely clear of the end of the tube.
steps.prose: All the way off its threads. A screw with one thread still engaged holds the barrel and invites a forced pull.
steps.quote: Loosen the take down screw by turning it counter clockwise until the screw threads are completely disengaged from the end of the magazine tube.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — BARREL REMOVAL, PDF p.7

steps.title: Barrel up and out with a gentle back-and-forth twist
steps.action: Work the barrel out of the receiver with a gentle back-and-forth rotation while pulling it up and out of the receiver assembly.
steps.prose: Gentle is the book's word. With the barrel off, leave the action alone: closing it hard or pulling the trigger now can damage the gun.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the receiver with a gentle back-and-forth rotational movement while pulling the barrel upward and out of the receiver assembly.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — BARREL REMOVAL, PDF p.7
steps.warn: Never forceably close the action or pull trigger while barrel is removed as damage could result to the firearm.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The barrel is off. That is the routine strip for this gun: bore, chamber and the exposed metal can all be cleaned now.
steps.prose: Mossberg's book goes on into the stock enclosure, the action and the receiver internals, but it warns first that this takes some expertise. That work is in Deep Clean, step by step from the book.
steps.quote: CAUTION: FURTHER DISASSEMBLY REQUIRES SOME EXPERTISE. IF IN ANY DOUBT, CONSULT A QUALIFIED GUNSMITH.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — BARREL REMOVAL, PDF p.7

steps.title: Barrel clean, then free of obstructions and excess oil
steps.action: Clean the bore and chamber with solvent and your cleaning kit, then make sure nothing is left in the barrel - no patch, no obstruction, no pooled lubricant.
steps.prose: Excess oil in a bore is an obstruction too. Look through it before it goes back on.
steps.quote: Make sure the barrel is free of obstructions and excessive lubricant after cleaning.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — CLEANING - METAL PARTS, PDF p.9

steps.title: Solvent on the metal, then a light coat of gun oil
steps.action: Clean all metal parts with gun solvent and give them a light coat of gun oil.
steps.prose: Light. Use a lubricant made for firearms.
steps.quote: All metal parts should be cleaned with gun solvent and lightly lubricated with gun oil.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — CLEANING - METAL PARTS, PDF p.9
steps.warn: Over lubrication should be avoided. Use only lubricants specifically designed for firearms.

steps.title: Trigger housing cleaned whole - only if Deep Clean has it out
steps.action: If the trigger housing is out of the receiver, clean it as one complete assembly with gun solvent and lubricate it lightly with gun oil.
steps.prose: It stays in one piece. Mossberg says it is a complex assembly that is not to be taken apart.
steps.quote: The trigger housing is a complex assembly and should not be disassembled. Clean as a complete assembly with gun solvent and lightly lubricate with gun oil.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — CLEANING - TRIGGER HOUSING, PDF p.9

steps.title: Plastic in mild soapy water; wet metal dried and oiled
steps.action: Clean the plastic parts with a mild solution of soap and water. Any metal that gets wet is dried thoroughly and lightly oiled.
steps.prose: Most of this gun's outside is plastic stock. Water on it is fine; water left on the steel is not.
steps.quote: All plastic components can be cleaned with a mild solution of soap and water. Should metal parts become wet, thoroughly dry and lightly lubricate all surfaces with gun oil.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — CLEANING - PLASTIC COMPONENTS, PDF p.10

deepSteps.title: Unloaded, crossbolt SAFE, barrel already off
deepSteps.action: Confirm the gun is unloaded and the crossbolt safety is fully to the right. The barrel comes off first, exactly as in the field strip.
deepSteps.prose: No force anywhere in what follows. If a part will not come free, stop and re-read the step.
deepSteps.quote: Make sure the gun is unloaded and that the crossbolt safety is in the "on" or "safe"(fully to the right) position.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY OF ACTION FROM PISTOL GRIP STOCK, PDF p.7
deepSteps.warn: If parts do not separate easily, reread appropriate directions and review parts diagram for proper parts orientation.

deepSteps.title: Phillips stock screw out of the centre of the pistol grip
deepSteps.action: Lay the gun on a clean, hard surface, ejection port up and pistol grip toward you. Take out the Phillips-head stock screw in the centre of the pistol grip.
deepSteps.prose: The lock nut on the far side comes loose when the screw is out - keep it with the screw.
deepSteps.quote: Loosen and remove Phillips head stock screw located in the center of the pistol grip. The grip screw lock nut on the opposite side is loose when stock screw is removed (Fig. 10).
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY, PDF p.7

deepSteps.title: Two screws out of the holes in the butt (5/32" hex)
deepSteps.action: Turn the gun so the recoil pad faces you and take out the two recoil and retaining screws inside the holes in the butt with the 5/32" hex wrench.
deepSteps.prose: They sit down inside the holes; the supplied wrench reaches them.
deepSteps.quote: Loosen and remove the two (2) recoil and retaining screws located inside the holes on the butt of gun (5/32" HEX head wrench required) (Fig. 10).
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY, PDF p.7

deepSteps.title: Two hex screws out of the pistol grip, nut held behind
deepSteps.action: With the 5/32" hex wrench, take out the two hex-head screws on the pistol grip. If the stock bolt nut on the far side turns with them, hold it with a flat-blade screwdriver.
deepSteps.prose: Five fasteners in all hold the stock halves together: one Phillips, two in the butt, two in the grip.
deepSteps.quote: Using a 5/32" HEX head wrench, loosen and remove the 2 Hex head screws on the pistol grip. It may be necessary to use a flatblade screwdriver to hold the stock bolt nut on the opposite side (Fig. 10).
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY, PDF p.7

deepSteps.title: Gun over, cup plate off the butt
deepSteps.action: Turn the gun over, ejection port down and pistol grip toward you, and pull the cup plate off the butt.
deepSteps.prose: It is held only by the squeeze of the two stock halves, so it can be stiff. Firm and straight, not pried.
deepSteps.quote: Turn the firearm over so that the ejection port is facing down and the pistol grip is facing you. Remove cup plate which is located on butt of gun. This piece is held on by friction fit with the two halves of the plastic housing and may require some force to remove.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY, PDF p.7

deepSteps.title: Forend forward, left enclosure lifted an inch and swung to 45 degrees
deepSteps.action: Move the forend all the way forward to the locked position. Steady the front of the gun with your left hand, take the rear of the stock enclosure in your right, lift it about an inch and swing it toward you. At about 45 degrees to the gun the left half lifts up and away.
deepSteps.prose: The crossbolt safety stays in the left enclosure as it comes off, and it is left there through cleaning and reassembly. Before anything else comes out, look at how the trigger parts sit - they must go back the same way.
deepSteps.quote: Lift rear of stock enclosure approximately one (1) inch and swing enclosure towards you. When the left hand stock enclosure is at a 45-degree angle to the gun, it is free to lift upward and away from the assembly (Fig. 11).
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY, PDF p.7
deepSteps.warn: NOTE: The crossbolt safety should remain with the left stock enclosure as it is removed. It should be left assembled throughout all assembly and cleaning procedures.

deepSteps.title: Recoil beam insert off the rear of the receiver (1/4" hex)
deepSteps.action: With the 1/4" hex wrench, turn the hex-head screw at the rear of the receiver counter-clockwise and take off the recoil beam insert.
deepSteps.prose: The trigger connector stays fastened to the trigger assembly for routine work. Its bars bend easily - keep tools and fingers off them.
deepSteps.quote: Using a 1/4" HEX head wrench, loosen and remove recoil beam insert located at rear of receiver by turning HEX head screw counter clockwise (Fig. 13).
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING OF ACTION ASSEMBLY, PDF p.8
deepSteps.warn: The trigger connector assembly should remain assembled to the trigger assembly during routine disassembly and cleaning procedures. Care must be taken so that the trigger connector bars are not bent (Fig. 13).

deepSteps.title: Receiver safety button fully rearward
deepSteps.action: Push the safety button on the top rear of the receiver fully rearward to its SAFE position.
deepSteps.prose: This is the receiver's own safety, hidden inside the stock - separate from the crossbolt. It has to be rearward for the elevator to come out later.
deepSteps.quote: Move the safety button located at the top rear of the receiver fully rearward to its "on" or "safe" position (Fig. 13).
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING OF ACTION ASSEMBLY, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Trigger housing pin out with a blunt punch, 3/16" or smaller
deepSteps.action: Trigger guard up on a clean surface. With a blunt punch no larger than 3/16", push out the small trigger housing retainer pin in the side of the receiver, about 1/2" below the rear of the trigger guard.
deepSteps.prose: Blunt, and no bigger than the book says, so the hole is not marked or opened up.
deepSteps.quote: With a blunt object (no greater than 3/16"[4.76 mm.] diameter), push out the small diameter trigger housing retainer pin located on the side of the receiver, approximately a 1/2" (12.7 mm.) below the rear of the trigger guard (Fig. 14).
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Trigger housing out, rear first - and it stays whole
deepSteps.action: Lift the trigger housing out of the receiver, rear end up first.
deepSteps.prose: That is as far as the housing goes. Taking it apart is factory or gunsmith work.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the trigger housing assembly by lifting the rear portion upward first.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, PDF p.8
deepSteps.warn: The trigger housing assembly is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled. Disassembly should only be performed by the factory or a qualified gunsmith.

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Do not drop the hammer with the housing out
deepSteps.action: Leave the trigger alone while the housing is out of the receiver. Letting the hammer fall on nothing can hurt you or damage the assembly.
deepSteps.prose: The hammer has to be fully cocked for the housing to go back in anyway.
deepSteps.quote: Do not pull the trigger and allow the hammer to fall when the trigger housing assembly is removed from the receiver. To do so may result in personal injury or damage to the assembly.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Trigger extension up and out; grip safety out with its plunger held
deepSteps.action: Pull the trigger extension straight up and out. Then, holding the plunger in, lift the grip safety up and out.
deepSteps.prose: The plunger is spring-loaded. Let go of it and it leaves.
deepSteps.quote: Lift out trigger extension by pulling upwards. While restraining plunger, lift grip safety upward and remove.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Primary trigger out - spring and washer held
deepSteps.action: Holding the spring and washer firmly, lift the trigger pin out of its slot in the trigger connector. Then slide the primary spring and washer off the trigger pin.
deepSteps.prose: The primary trigger is under spring tension. Keep a hand over the spring until it is off the pin.
deepSteps.quote: Primary trigger is under spring tension. Hold spring and washer securely, while lifting trigger pin from slot in trigger in connector. Remove primary spring and washer from trigger pin.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Trigger block and its spring out of the grip
deepSteps.action: Take the trigger block and the trigger block spring out of the grip portion of the stock. The spring is underneath the block.
deepSteps.prose: Small spring, easy to lose. The grip safety does not work without it.
deepSteps.quote: Remove trigger block and trigger block spring from inside grip portion of stock (spring is located under trigger block).
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Support spacer out, action and forend lifted from the right half
deepSteps.action: Take out the support spacer, then lift the action and forend together up and out of the right-hand stock enclosure.
deepSteps.prose: The action is now out of the stock in one piece, forend still on the magazine tube.
deepSteps.quote: The action and forend may now be lifted up and removed from the right-hand stock enclosure.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Inside of both stock halves - soap, water, soft brush, then bone dry
deepSteps.action: Clean the inside surfaces of both pistol grip stock halves with soap and water and a soft brush. Dry them completely before anything goes back in.
deepSteps.prose: Residue inside the stock is what slows the grip safety and trigger parts. Moisture left inside is the other problem.
deepSteps.quote: The inside surfaces of the two halves of the pistol grip stock should be thoroughly cleaned to insure proper functioning of internal parts. Residue may be removed with soap and water and a soft brush. BE CERTAIN ALL MOISTURE IS REMOVED BEFORE REASSEMBLING.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Cartridge interrupter and cartridge stop out
deepSteps.action: Take the cartridge interrupter out of the ejection-port side of the receiver and the cartridge stop out of the opposite side. A light tap on the sides of the receiver may free them.
deepSteps.prose: From here on, note how the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars sit together - they go back in the same relationship.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the cartridge interrupter from ejection port side and cartridge stop from opposite side. (It may be necessary to tap the sides of the receiver lightly to release these parts) (Fig. 15).
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, PDF p.9
deepSteps.warn: Pay special attention to the position of the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bar assembly during this portion of the disassembly, as the parts must be in the same relationship during reassembly.

deepSteps.title: Bolt three-quarters back, bolt slide lifted out at the clearance cuts
deepSteps.action: Move the forend and action slide back until the bolt and bolt slide are three-quarters of the way rearward. When the bottom of the bolt slide lines up with the clearance cuts in the receiver sides, lift the bolt slide up and out.
deepSteps.prose: It only comes out at that one position. If it will not lift, move the forend a little rather than forcing it.
deepSteps.quote: Move the forend/action slide assembly rearward so that the bolt assembly (Fig. 15) and bolt slide are three quarters of the way rearward. When the bottom of the bolt slide is aligned with the clearance cuts in the sides of the receiver, lift the bolt slide upward and out of the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, PDF p.9

deepSteps.title: Bolt forward out through the barrel opening
deepSteps.action: Slide the bolt assembly forward and out of the receiver through the barrel opening at the front.
deepSteps.prose: Forward, the way the barrel came out - not out the ejection port.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the bolt assembly (Fig. 1 6) by sliding it forward and out of the receiver assembly through the barrel opening at the front of the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, PDF p.9

deepSteps.title: Elevator pivoted up, arms squeezed, out
deepSteps.action: Pivot the front of the elevator up out of the receiver, squeeze its two open-end arms together until they clear their holes, and take the elevator out.
deepSteps.prose: The receiver's own safety button must be fully rearward for this, as set earlier.
deepSteps.quote: Pivot the front portion of the elevator upward out of the receiver. Squeeze the two arms, which form the open end of the elevator assembly, together sufficiently to disengage and remove the elevator from the receiver (Fig. 17).
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, PDF p.9
deepSteps.warn: The internal safety button located on the upper rear of the receiver must be in the "on" or "safe" (fully rearward) position to remove the elevator assembly (Fig. 16).

deepSteps.title: Forend and action slide forward off the magazine tube
deepSteps.action: Slide the forend and action slide assembly forward and off the magazine tube.
deepSteps.prose: That is everything the book takes apart.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the forend/action slide assembly by sliding it forward and off the magazine tube
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, PDF p.9

deepSteps.title: Stop here - the book's field disassembly is complete
deepSteps.action: Barrel, stock enclosure, recoil beam insert, trigger housing, trigger parts, action, cartridge stop and interrupter, bolt slide, bolt, elevator and forend are all out. Go no further.
deepSteps.prose: Mossberg says the shotgun is not to be taken further apart for routine cleaning or maintenance.
deepSteps.quote: Field disassembly is now completed!
deepSteps.cite: MOSSBERG OWNER'S MANUAL MODEL 500 BULL PUP — Model 500 Bullpup owner's manual (no part number or edition printed) — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, PDF p.9
deepSteps.warn: Consult the factory or a qualified gunsmith for further disassembly.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Bore and chamber cleaned with gun solvent and a quality cleaning kit
Barrel free of obstructions and excess lubricant before it goes back on
Never forcibly close the action or pull the trigger while the barrel is off

cleaning.name: METAL PARTS
tasks: All metal parts cleaned with gun solvent
A light coat of gun oil - lubricants made for firearms only

cleaning.name: TRIGGER HOUSING
tasks: Only if Deep Clean has it out: cleaned as one complete assembly in gun solvent
Do not disassemble the trigger housing
Do not pull the trigger with the housing out of the receiver

cleaning.name: PLASTIC COMPONENTS
tasks: Plastic parts cleaned with a mild solution of soap and water
Inside of both stock halves (Deep Clean): soap, water and a soft brush
Wet metal dried thoroughly and lightly oiled

reassembly: Field strip only: seat the barrel back in the receiver and turn the takedown screw clockwise onto the end of the magazine tube until it is snug - the reverse of the removal step. Do not force the action closed while the barrel is off.

Deep Clean, receiver first: receiver on a clean surface with the trigger opening up, the receiver's safety button fully rearward (SAFE). Slide the forend assembly onto the magazine tube, guiding the action slide bars into the cuts in the front and inside walls of the receiver.
Elevator: squeeze its arms together so the buttons drop into the 1/4" holes in the receiver, then pivot it until its forward part is even with the outside edge of the receiver cavity.

Bolt: rear end first, bolt lock downward toward the front inside top of the receiver, in through the barrel opening. Press the ejector (in the receiver wall opposite the ejection port) so the bolt slides fully rearward with the ejector in its slot in the bolt. Push the elevator down until it rests against the bolt.

Bolt slide: bolt rear even with the rear of the clearance cuts, action bars aligned. Fit the bolt slide rear end first, hook end down and forward, so it hooks into the cut under the bolt lock and the action bar slots. Hold it down and pull the forend forward - bolt and slide must move freely. If they do not, do not force it: take it apart and reassemble, watching how bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars relate.
Cartridge stop and cartridge interrupter onto the inside walls of the receiver, hooks facing inward toward the centre of the cavity.

Trigger housing: hammer fully cocked. Hold the cartridge stop and interrupter against the walls with one hand, fit the notches at the housing's front corners into the receiver slots and bring the rear down - do not force it. Line up the pin hole and push the trigger housing pin in flush. If it will not seat, check the housing's internal pins are flush and the stop and interrupter are positioned properly.

Receiver safety button forward to OFF. Recoil beam insert on the rear of the receiver, hex screw and washer tight, brass inserts facing the rear. Press the action lock lever and slide the forend slowly rearward then fully forward to check the parts move freely.

Ejection port up, trigger guard toward you: trigger connector flat bars resting on the side of the receiver, its roller against the trigger. Slide the right stock half (with the ejection-port cut) under the rear of the forend and rearward until the port cuts line up and the stock seats around the action with little front-to-back play.

Holding receiver and right stock half together, turn the gun over, ejection port down. Check the trigger connector is still in place. Trigger block spring into its hole in the trigger block; trigger block into the grip, smooth (spring) side down, thick end toward the muzzle. Press the thick end: released, it must spring back up. If it does not, the grip safety will not work and the gun is unsafe.

Spring and washer onto the grooved primary trigger pin; primary trigger into the stock with the trigger assembly slot in the pin's groove, washer and spring between the right stock wall and the trigger connector. Spring then plunger into the grip safety, and with the plunger held, grip safety into its cavity. Trigger extension onto its cuts in the primary trigger and down into its slot.

This copy of the book stops its assembly instructions at printed p.19; its printed pages 20-22 are not in it. The left stock enclosure (crossbolt safety still in it), the cup plate, the five stock screws and the barrel go back in the reverse of the order they came off. Anything that will not seat is not forced: Mossberg's advice is a qualified gunsmith or the factory.
